etymology_en: Ultimately from Proto-Indo-Iranian *čyáwatay, from Proto-Indo-European *kyew- (“to move, to go”). Related to Northern Kurdish çûn, çûyîn, Persian شدن (šodan, “to become, to go”), Ossetian цӕуын (cæwyn), Pashto شول (šwəl), Sanskrit च्यव॑ते (cyávate, “to move to and fro, to stir”), Old Armenian չու (čʻu) and Ancient Greek σεύω (seúō, “to put in quick motion, to drive”).
